question: Should OpenClaw adopt ordered immutable configuration layers with first-declaration ownership and narrowly enumerated monotonic exceptions as a permanent core configuration contract?
rationale: Tests and lifecycle proof can validate the proposed implementation, but they cannot decide whether this precedence and security-authority model is the long-term product contract OpenClaw should support.

options.title: Accept the narrow V1
options.body: Approve the startup-only, read-only contract and coordinate RFC acceptance with the linked implementation and compatibility validation.

options.title: Revise authority semantics
options.body: Keep both pull requests in draft while changing precedence, monotonic exceptions, diagnostics, or immutability guarantees.

options.title: Decline core layering
options.body: Keep configuration composition in the host integration rather than adding a permanent OpenClaw CLI and runtime contract.

recommendation.title: Accept the narrow V1
recommendation.body: Approve the startup-only, read-only contract and coordinate RFC acceptance with the linked implementation and compatibility validation.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline directly routes this RFC to the repository owner, and the unresolved choice concerns permanent core product and security semantics.
